sections.title: Why study Biomedical engineering in France?
sections.lead: \\Biomedical engineering\\ is the use of engineering, biology, medicine, electronics, materials science, and computing to create technologies that help in health care.

items: \\Major reasons to opt for Biomedical engineering in France are:\\
\\Specialised healthcare technology education\\: Learn about \\medical devices, clinical engineering, biomedical instrumentation, imaging, biomechanics and healthcare systems\.
\\Research opportunities:\\ Some universities and engineering schools collaborate with research labs, hospitals and healthcare technology organizations.
\\Interdisciplinary learning:\\ Students can combine engineering approaches with biology, physiology, electronics, computing and materials.
\\Industry exposure:\\ The programs may include laboratory projects, internships, industrial placements and work-study options.
\\Further study potential:\\ A bachelor's level science qualification can provide a pathway to a specialized master's degree or an engineering qualification, depending on the admission criteria.

sections.title: Biomedical Engineering courses in France
sections.lead: Different \\biomedical engineering courses in France\\ might have different titles. Options for explore include:

items: \\Biomedical Engineering - :\\ Devices for the medical sector, clinical engineering, biomedical instrumentation and health technologies.
\\Biomedical Science:\\ Human biology, human physiology, biomedical research and basic medical sciences.
\\Medical Technology and Health Engineering\\: Medical-device systems, healthcare equipment, electronics and digital health.
\\Biological Engineering:\\ Biotechnology, biological analysis, medical biology, lab application.
\\Health and Digital Engineering:\\ Biomedical uses of computing, electronics, data and connected medical systems.

sections.title: Eligibility to study Biomedical Engineering UG in France
sections.lead: \\Your eligibility to study biomedical engineering in France\\ is based on the program and whether you're applying for a bachelor's program or an engineering-school pathway.

items: Passed \\Class 12\\ or equivalent secondary-school qualification.
Strong grounding in \\mathematics and physics\\ for engineering-based courses.
Chemistry and biology preparation for biomedical science and biotechnology programs.
\\French language skills\\ for courses taught in French.
\\English language skills\\ for programs taught in the English language.
Satisfactory academic performance and any necessary entrance assessments.

The science subjects from Class 12 may be relevant for applicants from India. Mathematics and physics are particularly important for engineering programs and biology and chemistry can be important for biomedical science programs.
Some specialized biomedical engineering programs require \\two years of college\.

sections.title: Admission Requirements
sections.lead: Universities and engineering schools have their own \\ admission requirements \\ to evaluate candidates.

items: Secondary-school qualifications and transcripts recognized.
Sufficient preparation in \\math, physics, biology or chemistry.
Results of the French or English language test\\ where applicable. \]
Completed application form and supporting documentation.
A \\letter of motivation or personal statement\\ (if applicable).
Interview, entrance examination or academic assessment (if applicable).
Extra transcripts from higher education for applicants seeking to enter into an advanced year.

\\B2-level French\\ is a useful planning benchmark for French-taught courses, although the exact requirement will vary by program. Courses taught in English may require an accepted \\English-language test.\

sections.title: Application process
sections.lead: International students must follow \\the admission process for studying in France\\ applicable to their nationality, current country of residence and the institution they wish to attend.

items: 1. \\Choose your study track:\\ Go for a \\biomedical science bachelor's\\ or a longer \\biomedical engineering track\.
2. \\Check the qualification:\\ Look at the degree title, duration, language of instruction and accreditation.
3. \\Check entry requirements\\: Look at subject requirements , language requirements and direct entry after class 12.
4. \\Choose the application platform:\\ Depending on the program, applications are submitted via the institution's own portal.
5. \\Document Preparation:\\ Collect academic certificates, transcripts, language results, and any other documents requested.
6. \\Submit the application:\\ Submit the application before the deadline.
7. \\Go through the selection process:\\ If required, you may have to attend interviews or entrance exams.
8. \\Accept your offer:\\ Follow the instructions from the institution for registration and payment.
9. \\Visa and accommodation\\ If a \\France student visa\\ is required, make the
appropriate arrangements in plenty of time.

faqs.q: Can I pursue biomedical engineering in France after Class 12?
faqs.a: Yes but the routes are different. You can apply for an appropriate \\bachelor's degree programme\\ or a longer \\engineering route. Certain specialized courses in biomedical engineering require prior university training.

faqs.q: How long does it take to study biomedical engineering in France?
faqs.a: A \\Licence in biomedical sciences\\ usually takes three years. A full engineering-school pathway is typically five years after high school, depending on the program and the entry route.

faqs.q: Do I need French for biomedical engineering in France?
faqs.a: Many undergraduate courses are taught in French, and some require proof of \\French language proficiency. Before you apply, check the language of instruction and the tests they accept for each program.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to study biomedical engineering in France?
faqs.a: Biomedical engineering tuition fees in France vary by institution and qualification. The published public-university Licence reference for 2026–2027 is €178 a year for eligible French and EU students and €2,902 for non-EU students subject to differentiated fees. Fees for engineering-school and private-school can vary.

faqs.q: What will I do after I study biomedical engineering?
faqs.a: Career opportunities include medical device development, biomedical instrumentation, hospital equipment management, quality assurance, regulatory affairs, health technology, and research. Some specialist jobs require additional study or a qualification in engineering.
